x: Denis Merrett and Basil Walden were down as reserves for the 100 yards race, but as McDonald Bailey and Brian Shenton were present, their services were not required.

Dicky Bartlett ran 3rd in the 220 yds., which was won by Brian Shenton, and then came the sensation of the meeting, McDonald Bailey could only finish 3rd in the 100 yds. and was beaten by Ruddy of A.P.M., and our own Ron Holtum in 10.1 secs.
Only two Poly. runners put in an appearance, one being Brian Shenton, who won both the 100 and 220 yds. Basil Walden was 2nd in the 100 yds., and Dicky Bartlett was 3rd in the 220.

He won no less than 7 Berkshire A.A.A. titles at 100, 220 and 440 yards in the early 1950's and was a member of the Polytechnic 4 x 110 and 4 x 440 relay teams which includeded Macdonald Bailey, Arthur Wint and Brian Shenton, and which won A.A.A. titles.

Despite looking a finallist in the 100 metres, won by Bally of France, Brian Shenton, showing the best form of his life, repeated his 21.5 best performance in semis and final for a totally unexpected win in the 200 metres.
